description: A full cage of ribs, bleached and oddly intact. It came out of something that stopped needing lungs.
lore: Everything else on the counter is in pieces. That is what junk is — the bits that came apart. A cage comes off whole, spine and sternum and every rib still seated, and it stands up on the boards looking like the one intact thing in the room, and it will not sell that way.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] does the same thing every time. She looks at it, sets it on the floor, puts a boot through it, and pays the man the full price for it broken. She has never explained, the trade has stopped waiting for her to, and along that whole road it is simply how a cage is bought now. Twenty gold whole, twenty in pieces; the seller loses nothing, so everybody does it. Ask why and you get a shrug and four words. Because it was standing.
gm_notes: The one in this batch that is meant to stop the reader. Sigrun's reason is never given and should stay ungiven; the practice spread from her without anyone deciding it had. Do not connect it to the mountain on the page.
